label: Grounds of contingent concrete things precede them in time
definition: GroundsPrecedeAt h Concrete grounds v holds when, in history v, whenever y grounds a contingent concrete individual x under the supplied grounding relation at v and x is present at moment t, y is present at some moment strictly earlier than t. In ordinary language: whatever grounds a contingent thing was already there before each moment at which that thing is present. A thing appearing at time 1 grounded by something present at time 0 satisfies it; a thing sustained by a ground present only at the same moments does not.
note: Analyst formulation; attribution deferred. The grounding relation is the world-relative relation of BruteFoundationBoundary.Profile, not efficient causation of an event. The principle excludes grounding a contingent concrete thing only by a simultaneous ground; its rival is simultaneous (sustaining) grounding, as in a per se ordered series, which classical theists themselves typically accept. It is stronger than requiring one earlier ground: it constrains every ground. Applicability OPEN.
